facts.statement: Tylocephale is a genus of dinosaur.
facts.quote: genus: Tylocephale

facts.statement: The only known species of Tylocephale is T. gilmorei.
facts.quote: species: gilmorei

facts.statement: A partial skull and mandible of Tylocephale were unearthed in 1971 by a Polish-Mongolian Expedition in the Barun Goyot Formation of the Gobi Desert.
facts.quote: It is known from a partial skull and associated mandible that were unearthed in 1971 by a Polish-Mongolian Expedition to the Barun Goyot Formation of the Gobi Desert.

facts.statement: Tylocephale was described as a new genus and species in 1974 by Teresa Maryańska and Halszka Osmólska.
facts.quote: The specimen was described in 1974 by Polish paleontologists Teresa Maryańska and Halszka Osmólska as a new genus and species.

facts.statement: Tylocephale lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Mongolia.
facts.quote: that lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Mongolia.

facts.statement: Tylocephale means "swollen head" and is a genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur.
facts.quote: Tylocephale (meaning "swollen head") is a genus of pachycephalosaurid dinosaur

facts.statement: Tylocephale was average-sized for a pachycephalosaur, reaching 2 meters in length and 40 kilograms in body mass.
facts.quote: It was average-sized for a pachycephalosaur, reaching 2 m in length and 40 kg in body mass.

facts.statement: Tylocephale possesses the tallest known dome among pachycephalosaurs.
facts.quote: Tylocephale's dome is the tallest known from a pachycephalosaur.

facts.statement: An array of spikes, nodes, and tubercules protruded from behind the dome over the neck of Tylocephale.
facts.quote: Behind the dome, an array of spikes, nodes, and tubercules protrude posteriorly over the neck.

facts.statement: Serrations on Tylocephale's dentition imply a potentially heterogeneous diet including leaves, nuts, seeds, and insects.
facts.quote: Its dentition also bears serrations, implying a potentially more heterogeneous diet of leaves, nuts, seeds, and insects.

facts.statement: The rock layers of the Barun Goyot Formation, where Tylocephale was found, date to the Early Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 72 to 71 million years ago.
facts.quote: The rock layers of the Barun Goyot Formation derive from the Early Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, in numerical terms around 72 to 71 million years old.

facts.statement: The species name gilmorei honors American paleontologist Charles Gilmore for his first detailed description of a pachycephalosaur.
facts.quote: The species name honors American paleontologist Charles Gilmore, who wrote the first detailed description of a pachycephalosaur.

facts.statement: Unlike most dinosaurs which have three skull fenestrae, Tylocephale bears only two.
facts.quote: Most dinosaurs have three fenestrae (hollow spaces) in their skulls, but Tylocephale bears only two.

facts.statement: The jugals of Tylocephale possess giant, protruding, and irregularly spaced tubers.
facts.quote: Tylocephales jugals have giant, protruding, and irregularly spaced tubers.

facts.statement: The dome of Tylocephale had a rough texture, unlike in some other pachycephalosaurs.
facts.quote: The dome, unlike in some other pachycephalosaurs, had a rough texture.

facts.statement: The seven preserved teeth of Tylocephale have high crowns and arched cutting surfaces.
facts.quote: Teeth, seven in number, have high crowns and arched cutting surfaces.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Tylocephale's serrated dentition implies a heterogeneous diet including insects, nuts, and seeds in addition to plants.
facts.quote: Its dentition also bears serrations, implying a potentially more heterogeneous diet of leaves, nuts, seeds, and insects.

facts.statement: Tylocephale is classified as a member of the dinosaur group Pachycephalosauria.
facts.quote: Tylocephale was a member of the group Pachycephalosauria, a family of thick-skulled, herbivorous, bipedal dinosaurs

facts.statement: Pachycephalosaurs, including Tylocephale, are part of the larger group Marginocephalia.
facts.quote: Currently, pachycephalosaurs are recognized as being part of the larger group Marginocephalia which encompasses it and the gigantic, horned ceratopsians

facts.statement: A 2020 cladistic analysis suggested that pachycephalosaurs may extend back to the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: However, a 2020 cladistic analysis recovered the heterodontosaurids as an early branch of the group, which extend the age of pachycephalosaurs as far back as the Early Jurassic

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic analyses suggest Tylocephale is most closely related to Foraminacephale and Homalocephale.
facts.quote: Tylocephale specifically is most closely related to the dome-headed Foraminacephale and flat-headed Homalocephale according to most recent phylogenetic analyses

facts.statement: Some researchers have suggested that Tylocephale gilmorei is a synonym of Prenocephale prenes.
facts.quote: It has been suggested that instead of being its own species, Tylocephale gilmorei is a synonym of Prenocephale prenes

facts.statement: The genus Tylocephale was named by Maryańska and Osmólska in 1974.

facts.statement: Tylocephale fossils were discovered in the Khulsan locality of the Barun Goyot Formation, Mongolia, between 1965 and 1971.

facts.statement: Tylocephale is known only from a skull, which is the highest among pachycephalosaurids, and parts of the lower jaw.

facts.statement: Tylocephale measured approximately 2 meters in length and had a mass of about 40 kilograms.

facts.statement: Tylocephale's skull dome incorporated the postorbital and quadrate, and the temporal window may be absent due to a narrow parietosquamosal border.

facts.statement: Tylocephale lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 75 million years ago, in the Campanian stage.

facts.statement: Tylocephale lived during the Campanian stage, approximately 74 million years ago.

facts.statement: The time range for Tylocephale is estimated from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.

facts.statement: Tylocephale is endemic to the Barun Goyot Formation.

facts.statement: It has been suggested that Tylocephale had a back-and-forth jaw motion, differing from the up-and-down motion of Stegoceras.
facts.quote: However, it has been suggested that Tylocephale differed from Stegoceras by having a back-and-forth jaw motion instead of up-and-down

facts.statement: Tylocephale's dome is similar to Pachycephalosaurus, featuring fused sutures, mandibular and nasal tubercles, and expanded squamosal shelves.
facts.quote: Tylocephale's dome is most similar to Pachycephalosaurus with the presence of fused sutures, tubercules on the mandible and nasal, and expanded shelves on the squamosal

facts.statement: It is debated whether older individuals of pachycephalosaurs like Tylocephale could engage in head-butting due to less vascularized domes and potential healing issues.
facts.quote: The less vascularized domes of older pachycephalosaurs, and possibly diminished ability to heal from injuries, argued against such combat in older individuals

facts.statement: The Barun Goyot Formation, where Tylocephale lived, was deposited in alluvial plain, lacustrine, and aeolian environments under arid to semiarid climates.
facts.quote: The sediments of this formation were deposited in alluvial plain (flat land consisting of sediments deposited by highland rivers), lacustrine, and aeolian paleoenvironments, under relatively arid to semiarid climates
